basis: Operator decision 2026-10-20: proceed without a readable licence. Four channels were checked and agree that the City of Melbourne's data is open in intent but unstated in terms - the OpenDataSoft dataset metadata carries no licence field, the dataset page HTML carries no licence text, the open-data page describes an 'open-by-default' policy with five Open Data Principles but names no licence, its only relevant link (/copyright) speaks about website copyright, the /pages/terms URLs return 404, and the DataVic harvest of the same three datasets records license_id 'other-open' with license_url null. The operator was shown all of that and instructed: 'the license is fine. If they get mad they can just email me.' That is a risk acceptance by the dataset owner, not a publisher grant, and nothing in this file claims otherwise. This decision is specific to this candidate; it is not inherited by any other City of Melbourne dataset. If the City states terms, or asks us to stop, this file is where the change lands and release-manifest.py carries it into the manifest.

compilation.scope: Our contribution - the derived threshold target, the sensor/hour selection, the temporal partitions, the feature construction and the packaging - is offered under CC-BY-4.0 with attribution to the City of Melbourne. The dedication covers our contribution only. It does not relicense the source rows: those are redistributed as received from data.melbourne.vic.gov.au under terms the publisher has not stated, so no downstream licence is asserted over them and no standard licence is presented as the publisher's.

source.status: No licence stated by the publisher in any channel that could be read. Not public domain, not a standard open licence. Redistributed on the operator's recorded risk acceptance, with attribution and a working takedown path.
evidence: [OpenDataSoft catalog, read 2026-10-20] https://data.melbourne.vic.gov.au/api/explore/v2.1/catalog/datasets/pedestrian-counting-system-monthly-counts-per-hour - metas.default.license is null, license_url is null, records_count 1,626,831.
[Dataset page HTML, read 2026-09-18] no licence text node and no creativecommons.org link; the only 'license' occurrences are OpenDataSoft feature flags.

[City of Melbourne open-data page, read 2026-10-20 in a real browser - the earlier HTTP 403 was a user-agent block] https://www.melbourne.vic.gov.au/open-data describes an 'open-by-default' approach supported by five Open Data Principles and names no licence. Its only relevant outbound link is https://www.melbourne.vic.gov.au/copyright, which addresses website copyright and names no data licence or Creative Commons deed.
[Portal terms pages, read 2026-09-18] https://data.melbourne.vic.gov.au/pages/terms-of-use/ and /pages/terms/ return HTTP 404.

[DataVic CKAN harvest of the same three datasets, read 2026-10-20] https://discover.data.vic.gov.au/api/3/action/package_search?q=pedestrian+counting+system - license_id 'other-open', license_title 'other-open', license_url null, organization 'City of Melbourne'. A category, not terms.

[Operator decision, 2026-10-20] After those five findings were reported, the operator instructed: 'the license is fine. If they get mad they can just email me.' Recorded as a risk acceptance, not as a licence.

conditions: Attribution to the City of Melbourne ships in the README, the dataset card and the citation block.

The release carries a takedown route the publisher can actually use: the dataset card and README point to the public repository's issue tracker and to github.com/earino. A postal/email address is added at packaging time if the operator supplies one - no contact address is invented here.
No standard licence may be presented as the publisher's. The Hub card and site page say 'licence not stated by the publisher; our derived contribution is CC-BY-4.0'.
If the City states terms or asks for removal, the release is withdrawn or relicensed - this file is the single place that decision changes.
